text:
**Architecture overview.** sqlpipe moves Postgres data to S3 with three processes.

The reader process opens a Postgres connection and streams rows from the source table. It groups the rows into batches of a fixed size. Then it sends each batch to the converter.

The converter process receives one batch at a time. It maps the Postgres rows and types to Parquet columns. It writes each batch as one Parquet row group. Then it sends the row group to the uploader.

The uploader process writes the Parquet data to S3 as multipart objects. When a part upload fails, the uploader retries the part. After all parts are complete, the uploader finishes the multipart object.

The three processes run at the same time. As a result, sqlpipe reads, converts, and uploads in parallel.
